scores.label: Scoped WSG audit score
scores.formula: 100 * passed / (passed + failed + cantTell), grouped once per guideline

impactWeighted.status: Experimental project convention using WSG impact priority points; not a W3C site score

scores.interpretation: Passes satisfy only the declared scoped expectations; unknowns earn no points but are not defects. Compare only matching rubric, sample, and evidence profiles.

guidelines.title: Identify, assess, disclose, review, and mitigate sustainability impacts
guidelines.expectation: A retrieved public sustainability statement identifies the audited service and describes its impacts and mitigation. Judge disclosure only, not execution; an unresolved relationship is cantTell.

judgments.rationale: The retrieved wagtail.org/sustainability/ statement explicitly names guide.wagtail.org among projects whose impact and carbon emissions it is working to reduce. It describes climate impact, smaller image formats, image-generation features, dark mode and a sustainability roadmap, establishing service relationship and disclosed mitigation intent. Its ecosystem footprint figures are broader than this origin and do not measure the guide. The guide-local fallback routes return 404, but that does not negate the explicitly scoped parent statement. This passes disclosure only, not execution or quantified service-specific performance.
judgments.nextEvidence: Retrieve the complete roadmap and service-specific progress records to assess implementation; retain ecosystem and guide boundaries separately.

guidelines.title: Understand user requirements or constraints
Integrate sustainability into every stage of the ideation process
Design efficient and streamlined user journeys
guidelines.expectation: Execute declared task actions and inspect completion evidence; an expected selector is one observable, not proof of user success or optimal journey length.

judgments.rationale: The search task explicitly requires opening image-management guidance. Search opening and filling 'images' complete, but clicking the search-modal Manage images link times out after 5000 ms. The final URL is still /en/, its title remains Wagtail user guide and the only modal text is Search. successSelectorVisible=true does not establish task completion because Manage images already appears in homepage navigation. A separately loaded article proves content exists, not that this search journey succeeds. A selector/timing issue versus site search failure remains unresolved.
judgments.nextEvidence: Inspect the opened search results, input events and requests, then repeat with an observed result locator and sufficient loading evidence; require final article URL/title/content and compare the direct navigation path.

guidelines.title: Design to assist and not to distract
guidelines.expectation: Assess visible distractions against the declared visitor task; distinguish useful prompts from interruptions.

judgments.rationale: For finding image-management guidance, the homepage places a Wagtail Space conference promotion with attention-getting loudspeaker symbols before its task-category content (link y=569 at desktop). It competes with the editor's immediate task and is unrelated to managing images. The image article has no such promotion. The search modal is user-opened and therefore useful rather than an unsolicited interruption. This is a narrow content-priority failure, not evidence of engagement traps. The conference can benefit the Wagtail community, but its prominence before task routes is poorly matched to this specific editor task; this does not justify deleting event information site-wide.
judgments.nextEvidence: Compare a collapsed or less prominent conference notice with the existing homepage in an editor find-images task; verify discovery improves without hiding navigation.

guidelines.title: Avoid being manipulative or deceptive
guidelines.expectation: Inspect choice wording, defaults, prominence and the observed accept/reject paths for undue steering. DOM text alone does not establish visual parity.

judgments.rationale: Both staged branches report no_banner and page snapshots show no consent overlay or accept/reject controls. Ordinary choices include theme, language and article feedback; no pressure wording is evident in the captured text. Their alternative paths, defaults and visual prominence were not exercised or visually compared, so the declared choice-path expectation remains unresolved. Absence of a banner is not itself a defect.
judgments.nextEvidence: Exercise theme, language and helpfulness alternatives and inspect screenshots and persistent defaults; assess consent paths only if a consent prompt is encountered.

guidelines.title: Make deliverables understandable and reusable
guidelines.expectation: Assess the sampled task's wording, headings and terminology for its stated audience; retain uncertainty about unrepresented users.

judgments.rationale: For the stated Wagtail-editor audience, 'Manage images' matches the task and the article separates adding/editing/removing images, alt text, focal area, formats and file limits with descriptive headings. Instructions name the Images sidebar, edit screen, Save and Remove focal area controls; focal area and alt text are explained rather than left as unexplained jargon. The warning clearly states that changing an image file changes every page using it. This supports the sampled wording expectation, with no claim about comprehension for unrepresented users.
judgments.nextEvidence: Validate the instructions with novice editors and an actual Wagtail image-upload task, including users unfamiliar with image formats.

guidelines.title: Use a design system for interface consistency
guidelines.expectation: Compare repeated navigation and control names across sampled pages; consistent samples do not prove a documented design system.

judgments.rationale: The homepage and Manage images article repeat the same navigation taxonomy, including Manage documents, Manage images and Manage snippets, and the same search ('Toggle the search form'), theme ('Toggle between dark and light theme'), Copy page and English controls. The article title agrees with its navigation link and previous/next labels. This supports repeated naming across the two sampled pages; it does not establish ownership or existence of a documented design system.
judgments.nextEvidence: Extend comparison to other guide sections and opened menus; request component documentation only for a broader design-system judgment.

guidelines.title: Optimize media to reduce resource use
Ensure animation is proportionate and easy to control
guidelines.expectation: Assess observed animation purpose, playback controls and reduced-motion behavior. A quiet snapshot does not prove no motion occurs elsewhere.

judgments.rationale: Both pages report zero active animations and no audio/video in desktop and live reduced-motion states; reducedMotion changes from false to true. No animation is captured whose purpose, playback controls or changed motion behavior can be assessed. The user-opened search state also does not establish transition behavior. Quiet short snapshots cannot resolve animation over interaction and scrolling.
judgments.nextEvidence: Observe search, mobile menu, theme and feedback transitions with and without reduced motion, including timing and any controls for sustained motion.

guidelines.title: Use optimized web typography
Avoid unwanted notifications
guidelines.expectation: Assess observed alerts and notification permission requests for user value and choice; absence is limited to observed states.

judgments.rationale: No permission request calls are observed (requestCalls=0) and no unsolicited notification or alert appears in the sampled initial, narrow, reduced-motion, print, no-JavaScript or search states. The search overlay follows an explicit click and is useful for the declared task. This is a scoped absence of unwanted notifications, not proof about later sessions. Browser permission is already denied, so permission-prompt behavior in a fresh default-permission profile remains outside this result.
judgments.nextEvidence: Repeat the task with notification permission initially default and inspect any subsequent feedback/subscription flow before expanding the scope.

guidelines.title: Reduce the impact of downloadable and physical documents
guidelines.expectation: Review print layout visibility and download labels for the declared task. Fetch and inspect document content before asserting optimization or equivalence.

judgments.rationale: The task guidance is HTML and no download links are detected, so there is no sampled downloadable file whose labeling or optimization can be judged. Print emulation retains the task headings and all four article images while removing the main sidebar (article navigation count falls from two to one, consistent with its contents navigation remaining). Search, theme and copy controls remain visible in print observations, and actual pagination and paper use were not inspected. These facts do not establish an efficient printable document.
judgments.nextEvidence: Generate print previews for both pages and inspect pagination, clipped text, image legibility and redundant controls; inspect any download content if a download is later found.

guidelines.title: Involve users early in the project
Audit and test for bugs or issues requiring resolution
Validate usability through testing and real-world usage
Provide cross-platform compatibility support
Set goals based on performance and energy impact
Minify and remove unused code
guidelines.expectation: Use initial JS/CSS execution observations to nominate investigation targets; require representative journeys or source corroboration before recommending removal.

judgments.rationale: Initial coverage contains unexecuted ranges in the shared main JavaScript bundle and jsi18n translation helpers, alongside CSS rule-usage observations. Main script source length is 89,576 positions, not transferred bytes. Search, theme, copying, language and article feedback are later-use candidates, and the search journey did not complete. Initial nonexecution therefore nominates bundle/helper investigation but does not demonstrate dead code or justify deletion.
judgments.nextEvidence: Capture coverage through successful search, mobile navigation, theme, copy, language and feedback journeys, then corroborate remaining unused ranges against deployed source before removal.

guidelines.title: Modularize bandwidth-heavy components
guidelines.expectation: Relate initial script resources to visible components and later task needs; recommend splitting only when a component's deferred use and usable activation are corroborated.

judgments.rationale: Both pages initially request the shared main script, blocking script and language catalog. Visible later-use features include search, theme, Copy page and language options, while the article adds feedback. No video or other clearly bandwidth-heavy embedded component is present. Search opens but its result click times out, and neither module boundaries nor usable deferred activation is established; splitting recommendations would be premature.
judgments.nextEvidence: Inspect deployed bundle composition and successful feature activation with request timing; split only a material optional component whose deferred loading retains usable activation.

guidelines.title: Avoid redundancy and duplication in code
Treat third parties the same as first parties
Ensure code follows good semantic practices
Defer the loading of non-critical resources
Structure metadata for machine readability
Use media queries that support sustainability goals
Ensure layouts work for different devices and requirements
guidelines.expectation: Compare narrow and desktop task content and overflow, then exercise affected controls; width emulation alone is not real-device compatibility.

judgments.rationale: At 1280 and 360 CSS pixels both pages retain their task headings, the article retains four images, and horizontalOverflow is false; the main sidebar is hidden at narrow width and a Mobile menu toggle appears. However, that menu and other affected controls were not exercised. The homepage narrow English control begins at x=316.48 with width=91.02, extending beyond the 360-pixel viewport despite the overflow flag, a concrete clipping concern requiring visual and interaction checks. These snapshots cannot establish device compatibility.
judgments.nextEvidence: At 360 pixels, inspect language/copy toolbar clipping and activate language, search and the mobile menu; complete the find-images task on a real touch device and with keyboard navigation.

guidelines.title: Use sustainable JavaScript and APIs
Use dependencies sparingly and maintain them
Include expected and beneficial files
guidelines.expectation: The sampled service exposes a discoverable, parseable carbon.txt with usable declared relationships. Missing carbon.txt is a scoped absence, not proof of high emissions or failure of the entire guideline. Judge redirects, delegation, supported versions and schema findings explicitly.

judgments.rationale: Root /carbon.txt and /.well-known/carbon.txt both return 404 HTML without redirects or Carbon-Location delegation; the successful homepage also supplies no Carbon-Location. DNS discovery is recorded as queried and no file relationship is established. Thus the sampled discovery routes do not expose the expected parseable file. With no retrieved carbon.txt there is no declared version, TOML syntax, schema or provider relationship to validate. This is a scoped file absence, not high emissions or failure of all guideline 3.13.
judgments.nextEvidence: Publish or locate a carbon.txt relationship for this origin, then validate its supported version, syntax/schema, service domains and evidence links through the same discovery routes.

guidelines.title: Use the most efficient solution for your service
Use the latest stable language version
Reduce the number and complexity of database queries
Use sustainable hosting
guidelines.expectation: Hosting claims identify provider, service and supporting evidence with a relationship to this origin. Self-declaration without independently corroborated operational scope remains cantTell for sustainable hosting; do not set SWDM green-hosting flags from this check.

judgments.rationale: No carbon.txt record identifies a provider/service relationship for guide.wagtail.org, and the retrieved sustainability statement describes CMS/community mitigation rather than independently corroborated hosting operations for this origin. The ecosystem footprint article concerns thousands of Wagtail sites, not this service's provider, electricity or infrastructure. Sustainable hosting therefore remains unknown; no green-hosting model flag follows from public intent or domain association.
judgments.nextEvidence: Obtain the origin's current hosting provider and service relationship plus dated independent operational evidence covering the actual infrastructure and electricity supply.

guidelines.title: Optimize caching and support offline access
Reduce data transfer with compression
Setup necessary error pages and redirection links
Avoid maintaining unnecessary virtualized environments or containers
Use automation wisely
Define the frequency of data refreshes
Back up critical data at routine intervals
Assess the impact and requirements of data processing
Use Content Delivery Networks (CDNs) when beneficial
Ensure infrastructure fits project requirements
Store data according to the needs of your users
Have an ethical and sustainable product strategy
Assign a sustainability advocate
Inform, raise awareness, and train for sustainability
Communicate the environmental impact of user choices
guidelines.expectation: Identify consequential user choices in the sample and assess whether contextual impact information is useful and supported. Do not prescribe carbon labels on every control.

judgments.rationale: The declared visitor task is finding and reading image-management documentation. The sampled site offers navigation, search, copying, theme, language and feedback, but no consequential download, media-quality, purchase or upload decision requiring a contextual environmental comparison. The article discusses upload limits and developer-configured image compression, but it is guidance about a separate CMS workflow, not an upload choice on this service. No need for carbon labels on these reading controls is established.
judgments.nextEvidence: If scope expands to an actual upload, download or media-selection workflow, identify its meaningful resource tradeoffs and assess useful, substantiated contextual information there.
